title: Edge connectivity is at most the minimum degree
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with at least one vertex. Then the edge connectivity of $G$ is at most its minimum degree; that is, $\kappa'(G) \le \delta(G)$, where $\delta(G)$ denotes the least degree of any vertex of $G$.
hypotheses_covered: at least one vertex (nonempty vertex set)
replaced:
Second inequality: \texttt{$\kappa$' $\le$ $\delta$}.

$\kappa \leq \kappa' \leq \delta$.

The inequalities in theorem 3.1 are often strict. For example, the graph $G$ of figure
3.2 has $\kappa = 2$, $\kappa' = 3$ and $\delta = 4$.
